    //==
    // # Quadric decimation
    //
    // Coarsening driven by the error quadrics above: an edge's cost is the value
    // of the summed quadric of its two endpoints at the point that minimizes it,
    // and the cheapest edges collapse first.
    //
    // In a mutable decimator the candidate edges live in a priority queue that is
    // updated after every collapse. Here a pass ranks every edge against the same
    // mesh, collapses the cheapest non-adjacent set of them, and the next pass
    // ranks again — which recomputes more than a queue would, and needs no queue,
    // no lazy invalidation and no re-heapification.

    // Where the collapse of an edge should put its surviving vertex: the minimizer
    // of the summed quadric, falling back to the midpoint where the system is
    // singular.
    EdgeCollapseTarget(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, quadrics: Array<Quadric>, e: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var midpoint = self.EdgeMidpoint(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        return quadrics[pair.A.Value].Add(quadrics[pair.B.Value]).QuadricMinimizer(midpoint);
    }

    // What collapsing an edge costs: the summed quadric evaluated at the point the
    // collapse would move to.
    EdgeCollapseCost(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, quadrics: Array<Quadric>, e: Integer): Number
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var summed = quadrics[pair.A.Value].Add(quadrics[pair.B.Value]);
        return summed.QuadricError(self.EdgeCollapseTarget(topology, quadrics, e));
    }

    // The rank of one cost among all of them, ties broken by position so that the
    // ranks are a permutation. This is how "the k cheapest" is selected without a
    // sort: an edge is among the k cheapest exactly when its rank is below k.
    // Quadratic in the edge count.
    CostRank(costs: Array<Number>, i: Integer): Integer
        => costs.Count.MapRange(j =>
            (costs[j] < costs[i]).Or((costs[j] == costs[i]).And(j < i)) ? 1 : 0)
            .Reduce(0, (acc, hit) => acc + hit);

    // One decimation pass: rank every edge by quadric error and collapse the
    // `budget` cheapest of them that pass the collapse rules and do not cross the
    // boundary. Materially fewer than `budget` collapses land, because no two may
    // have adjacent endpoints; that is what makes several passes the normal way to
    // use this.
    DecimationPass(self: TriangleMesh3D, budget: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var quadrics = self.VertexQuadrics;
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        var costs = topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => self.EdgeCollapseCost(topology, quadrics, e));
        return self.CollapseEdges(topology,
            topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
                (CostRank(costs, e) < budget)
                    .And(CrossesBoundary(boundary, topology.UndirectedEdges[e]).Not)),
            e => self.EdgeCollapseTarget(topology, quadrics, e));
    }

    // Decimation toward a target face count. Each pass asks for half the remaining
    // excess in collapses — an accepted collapse removes about two triangles — but
    // the conflict rule accepts only a fraction of what it is asked for, so
    // `passes` is a budget rather than a guarantee and the count approaches the
    // target from ABOVE. Ten to twenty passes reach a target well under half the
    // input; raising the budget does not substitute for raising the pass count,
    // because the limit is conflicts and not the ranking.
    Decimated(self: TriangleMesh3D, targetFaceCount: Integer, passes: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => Repeat(passes, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, pass) =>
            mesh.DecimationPass(((mesh.Faces.Count - targetFaceCount) / 2).Max(0)));

    // Decimation under an error bound: every edge whose quadric error is at or
    // below `maxError` is a candidate, and passes run until the budget is spent.
    // The bound is in squared distance units, because a quadric accumulates
    // SQUARED distances.
    DecimatedToError(self: TriangleMesh3D, maxError: Number, passes: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => Repeat(passes, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, pass) => mesh.DecimationErrorPass(maxError));

    // One pass of error-bounded decimation.
    DecimationErrorPass(self: TriangleMesh3D, maxError: Number): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var quadrics = self.VertexQuadrics;
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        return self.CollapseEdges(topology,
            topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
                (self.EdgeCollapseCost(topology, quadrics, e) <= maxError)
                    .And(CrossesBoundary(boundary, topology.UndirectedEdges[e]).Not)),
            e => self.EdgeCollapseTarget(topology, quadrics, e));
    }

    //==
    // # Isotropic remeshing
    //
    // The Botsch-Kobbelt loop (https://doi.org/10.1145/1057432.1057457): given one
    // target edge length, repeatedly split what is too long, collapse what is too
    // short, flip toward valence six, and relax tangentially. The 4/3 and 4/5
    // factors are theirs — splitting above 4/3 L and collapsing below 4/5 L is what
    // keeps the two operations from undoing each other, since a split edge lands at
    // 2/3 L and a collapse cannot then immediately re-shorten it.
    //
    // Every one of the four steps rebuilds the connectivity it needs, so a pass
    // costs four topology builds. That is the price of writing the loop as a
    // composition of independently meaningful operations rather than as one
    // traversal that maintains a structure.

    // One iteration of the Botsch-Kobbelt loop at the given target edge length.
    IsotropicRemeshPass(self: TriangleMesh3D, targetEdgeLength: Number): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.SplitLongEdges(targetEdgeLength * 4.0 / 3.0)
            .CollapseShortEdges(targetEdgeLength * 4.0 / 5.0)
            .FlipTowardValenceSix
            .TangentiallyRelaxed(0.5, 1);

    // A mesh remeshed toward uniform edges of the given length. One pass halves an
    // over-long edge and takes one non-adjacent round of short edges out, so a mesh
    // far from the target needs several: five iterations to refine, ten or more to
    // coarsen (collapses conflict where splits do not). The boundary is preserved
    // throughout.
    IsotropicRemeshed(self: TriangleMesh3D, targetEdgeLength: Number, iterations: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
        => Repeat(iterations, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, pass) => mesh.IsotropicRemeshPass(targetEdgeLength));

    // The average length of the undirected edges of a mesh: the natural starting
    // point for a target edge length, and what a caller scales up or down to
    // coarsen or refine.
    AverageEdgeLength(self: TriangleMesh3D): Number
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return topology.EdgeCount.IsZero
            ? 0.0
            : topology.EdgeCount
                .MapRange(e => self.EdgeLength(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)))
                .Reduce(0.0, (acc, len) => acc + len) / topology.EdgeCount.ToNumber;
    }
}
